sections.heading: A Cut That Gets Better Every Visit
body: Most barbers aim to repeat the last cut. That's the floor here, not the goal.

A haircut wears differently than it looks in the chair. It sits one way with a collared shirt and another with a hoodie. It feels different at work, on a weekend and after a week of Missouri humidity.
So each visit starts with how the last one wore.
What did you like by day ten? What bugged you? Did the top fall the way you wanted with what you actually wear?
Ash takes that in and adjusts. A little more off the crown, a softer line at the neck, a fade that sits lower. Visit by visit, the cut moves toward the one that's really yours.
You get the cut you ask for every time. You also get a barber who keeps working on it with you.

sections.quote: Just moved to this Ozark Community from Kansas. Needed a barber to take care of my hair needs...Can't say enough about Ash, fantastic barber and great for conversation.

sections.heading: Haircuts and Fades
body: The grown-out fade is the haircut moment everyone knows. A week after the cut, the sides have lost their shape and you're looking at the calendar.
A fade is a blend. The hair goes from short at the bottom to longer on top with no line where one length stops and the next begins.
That is why a bad fade is so obvious. A rushed blend shows a step, and as it grows out the shape falls apart faster than it should. A clean one grows out evenly, and you can keep the look for weeks.
We cut classic barber haircuts, tapers, and fades low, mid and high. Skin fades and clean necklines are part of the same work. Show us the photo and we'll match the guard lengths and the line.

sections.quote: Best haircut I've gotten, the fade she does is crazy good, I will definitely be going back

sections.heading: Kids and Teens
body: Some kids dread the chair. They squirm, they hate the sound of clippers, or the last haircut left them with something they never asked for.

We ask the kid what they want, not just the parent, and we cut it. A kid who sees the barber listening sits still longer, and a kid who likes the result asks to come back. Teens get the same fades and tapers as the adults in the next chair.
Cowlicks, a first haircut and a toddler who won't hold still are all normal for us. The kids' page covers how a visit goes and what to do before you come in.

sections.heading: Beard Trim, Cut and Shaping
body: A beard grows out of shape slowly, so you don't notice until the cheek line has drifted, the neck has gone fuzzy and one side is longer than the other.
Trimming, cutting and shaping are three different jobs.
A trim keeps your length and tidies it.

A cut takes the beard shorter. Shaping sets the cheek line and neckline so the edges look deliberate. We do all three, and we can do them in the same visit as your haircut so the lines on your head and your face match.

sections.heading: When a Beard Needs a Trim
body: You can usually tell. One side is longer than the other, stray hairs run down the neck and the edge along your cheek has blurred.
Hair grows at different speeds on different parts of the face, so a beard loses its shape faster than the hair on your head. A beard that is the right length can still look unfinished.
A trim fixes that without changing how your beard looks. The length stays, the surface evens out, and the edges come back.

sections.heading: Trim, Cut and Shaping: Which One Do You Need?
body: These three terms get mixed up, so here is how we use them.
**Beard trim.** Maintenance. Your beard keeps about the same length. We even out the surface, clean up stray hairs and tidy the edges.
**Beard cut.** A change in length. If the beard has grown past where you like it, or you want to go from full to short, a cut takes real length off and gives you a new starting point.
**Beard shaping.** The lines. We set the cheek line and the neckline so the beard has clear edges.
Most men want a mix.
A long beard may need a cut and then shaping. A short one may only need a trim. Tell us what you're after when you sit down and we'll build the right combination.

sections.heading: Which One to Book
list: The length is right but it looks messy: a beard trim.
It's longer than you want, or you want a new length: a beard cut.
The length is fine but the edges aren't clean: beard shaping.
You want a different look overall: a cut with shaping.
tail: If you can't tell which is which, show up and say so. We'll look at the beard and tell you what it needs.

sections.heading: Haircut and Beard in One Visit
body: Book a haircut and beard work together and the same barber cuts both, so the lines match. The sides of your haircut can blend into the beard, a fade into the beard with no hard break at the sideburn.
Tell us you want both when you book, and we'll set aside the time.

sections.heading: Getting Ready for Your Appointment
body: Come in with the beard you have. You don't need to comb it into shape or trim it first. A beard trimmed at home the night before is harder to shape, because the uneven spots hide the way it naturally grows.
A photo of the look you want helps a lot. Point out any cowlick, patchy spot or thin side so we can work around it.

sections.heading: Patchy and Thin Spots
body: Many beards run thick at the chin and thin out on the cheeks. A beard like that looks best with a length and a line chosen around the patches, not in spite of them.
We look at where the beard is full and where it's sparse, then pick a shape that makes it look full.

sections.heading: Beard Oil
body: Ash keeps a collection of beard oils at her station in the shop. Ask about them when you're in the chair.

items.q: Can I get a beard trim without a haircut?
items.a: Yes. Book it on its own or add it to a haircut.

items.q: What's the difference between a trim and a cut?
items.a: A trim keeps your length and cleans up. A cut takes the beard shorter.

items.q: Can you shape a beard that has grown out?
items.a: Yes. If it has also grown past the length you like, we cut it down and then shape it.

items.q: How often should I come in?
items.a: It depends on how fast you grow and how sharp you like the edges. Many men with a shaped beard come every few weeks, and you can plan your schedule with us after your first visit.

items.q: How do I book beard work?

sections.heading: Why Kids Fight the Chair
body: A haircut is odd for a child. Someone they don't know stands behind them with buzzing clippers near their ears and tells them not to move.
Add a quick cut that skips what they asked for and you get a kid who dreads next time. It isn't stubbornness. It's a reasonable reaction to a bad few minutes.
The fix is a barber who slows down, talks to the kid instead of over them and works with the head they actually have.

sections.heading: What We Do Differently
body: We ask your child what they want. A five-year-old can tell us "short on the sides" or "like my dad's," and a teen can show us a photo. Then we cut that.
We stay engaged with the kid through the whole cut. Talking while we work keeps small kids calm, and it lets us check that the haircut is going the way they pictured it.
The result is a child who sits in the chair because they know what's coming and they like how they look when it's done.

sections.quote: Excellent customer service. She did a great job on my son's hair. Very engaged with him during his appointment.

sections.heading: Cowlicks, Part Lines and Hair That Won't Behave
body: Cowlicks are patches of hair that grow in a different direction from the rest. Kids have them at the crown, at the front hairline and behind the ears, and they decide how a cut lies.
Cut against a cowlick without noticing and the hair sticks up all week. A barber who sees it first leaves the hair longer there, or cuts with the direction it grows, so the style sits flat.
A hard part is a shaved line that separates the top from the side. On a child with several cowlicks it takes patience to get straight.

sections.quote: My son is 5 and Ash did such a good job on his hair. He's got multiple cowlicks. She did his hard-part expertly and blended everything beautifully. Very thorough, with awesome attention to detail.
sections.name: Josie M.

sections.heading: Toddlers and First Haircuts
body: Toddlers don't know what a haircut is. They know the chair is high, the cape is strange and the clippers are loud.
We cut toddlers' hair, and a first haircut is a normal visit for us. Tell us it's a first when you book or when you sit down so we can go at the pace your child sets.
A few things help any small child.
Tell them ahead of time that they'll sit in a big chair and the barber will trim their hair, and that it doesn't hurt. Bring them when they're rested and fed. Stay where they can see you.

sections.quote: I bring my toddlers here too, and she's amazing with them.

sections.heading: Teen Cuts: Fades, Tapers and Photos
body: Teens have opinions about their hair, and they should. Let them pick the cut. A teenager who chose the style wears it better than one who got whatever a parent picked.
Most teen styles are a taper or a fade.

A taper gets gradually shorter toward the neck and around the ears. A fade blends the sides from longer down to very short, and a skin fade takes the bottom down to the skin. The top can stay longer and textured so it holds a style.
If your teen doesn't know what the cut is called, a photo works. We turn it into the right guard lengths and the right blend, and finish with a clean neckline.

sections.heading: Booking for More Than One Kid
body: Book each child a separate time, back to back, and tell us you're coming together. A parent can book a haircut or a beard trim in the same stretch, so you get everyone done in one trip. Say what you want when you book and we'll set aside the time.

However customers find you, a Google search, a friend's recommendation or a quick look before booking a chair, it all ends in the same place.

Right now people find Ash's Barber Collective through the Google listing and the Square booking link. There's no website yet, so there's nowhere to see the work, read what makes your cuts different, or find the kids and beard services.
So we built the pages a customer looks for first, around what your regulars already say: the cut gets better every visit.
